correctness.rationale: The local criterion of almost-uniform distribution modulo every prime-ideal power is correctly used for all n+1 points. For a hypothetical six-point n=5 optimal set, all pair differences must avoid primes with norm>=6 and squares of the two primes of norms 3 and 4, forcing norm in {1,3,4,12} by unique factorization. Translation fixes zero and confines five nonzero points to the exact 24 Eisenstein neighbors; 4N=(2a-b)^2+3b^2 bounds coordinates, so enumerating all C(24,5)=42504 subsets is complete. Independent recomputation found 54 pairwise norm-compatible rooted choices with three profile types: 12 have 3-residue (2,2,2) but 4-residue (1,1,1,3); 36 have (1,2,3) and (1,1,2,2); six have (0,3,3) and (0,2,2,2). None balances both. Four explicit witnesses have all necessary small-prime profiles and pairwise norm restriction, hence are balanced for every larger prime-power modulus. A six-point 5-universal set would be 5-optimal; published Byszewski–Frączyk–Szumowicz n+2 upper bound gives seven. The latter external theorem is credited, not independently proved.

value.rationale: Earliest failure of simultaneous p-ordering in a concrete imaginary quadratic integer ring is a natural arithmetic threshold. The obstruction isolates incompatibility between norm-3 and inert norm-4 residue distributions and gives the sharp minimal degree-five universal-set cardinality. This is not a trivial consequence of eventual nonexistence and does not depend on an arbitrary coordinate slice.

final_claim: In Eisenstein integers Z[omega], prime-ideal balanced n-optimal interpolation sets exist for n=1,2,3,4 but no six-point n=5 set exists; the degree-five universal-set minimum is exactly seven by the general n+2 theorem.
limitations: Only first five positive degrees; no claim that all higher degrees fail, nor an explicit construction of seven-point degree-five set beyond the cited existence theorem.
